message:
Fixes #19280

## Summary

Test runner flags are now exposed via a `testFlags` object on the `bun:test` import, providing a clean, type-safe API for accessing test configuration at runtime.

## Problem

Previously, test runner flags were consumed by the argument parser and not accessible to test code, making it impossible for tests to check if certain flags were enabled.

For example, when running:
```bash
bun test --update-snapshots
```

There was no way for test code to detect whether snapshot updates were requested.

## Solution

This PR exposes all test configuration through a `testFlags` object exported from `bun:test`:

```typescript
import { testFlags } from "bun:test";

console.log(testFlags.updateSnapshots); // true when --update-snapshots is passed
console.log(testFlags.seed);            // actual seed value when --randomize is used
```

### Available Properties

The `testFlags` object includes:
- `defaultTimeout: number` - Current default timeout in milliseconds
- `updateSnapshots: boolean` - Whether snapshot updates are enabled
- `rerunEach?: number` - Number of times to rerun each test
- `runTodo: boolean` - Whether to run todo tests
- `only: boolean` - Whether to run only `.only` tests
- `passWithNoTests: boolean` - Whether to pass when no tests are found
- `concurrent: boolean` - Whether tests run concurrently
- `randomize: boolean` - Whether to randomize test order
- `seed?: number` - **Resolved** random seed for test order
- `bail?: number` - Number of failures before stopping
- `testFilterPattern?: string` - Pattern to filter tests
- `maxConcurrency: number` - Maximum number of concurrent tests

### Resolved Values

The `randomize` and `seed` properties reflect the **actual runtime values**, not just the CLI options. When `--randomize` is used without an explicit `--seed`, Bun generates a random seed internally, and `testFlags.seed` will contain that generated value, making it easy to reproduce test runs.

## Implementation

**Modified `src/bun.js/test/jest.zig`:**
- Added `seed` field to `TestRunner` struct to store resolved seed value
- Added `createTestFlags()` function to build the JavaScript testFlags object
- Modified `createTestModule()` to export the `testFlags` object

**Modified `src/cli/test_command.zig`:**
- Pass the resolved seed value to `TestRunner`

## Testing

Comprehensive test coverage in `test/js/bun/test/test-flags.test.ts` with 12 tests verifying:
- ✅ Boolean flags (updateSnapshots, only, runTodo, concurrent, randomize, etc.)
- ✅ Optional numeric flags (bail, rerunEach)
- ✅ String flags (testFilterPattern)
- ✅ Resolved seed when using `--randomize`
- ✅ Explicit seed value when using `--seed`
- ✅ All property types are correct

All tests pass successfully.

## Example Usage

```typescript
import { test, expect, testFlags } from "bun:test";

test("snapshot test", () => {
  if (testFlags.updateSnapshots) {
    // Update snapshot logic
  }
  
  // Use the actual seed for debugging
  if (testFlags.randomize) {
    console.log(`Tests running with seed: ${testFlags.seed}`);
  }
});
```
